why: Rule 1 at the only real junction in a 25-cluster dust event: both measured prongs off deg-3 12004 cool toward it (58k->111k to 12001, 39k->52k to 12005) and the third is flat.
Only rule-1 support in the event (2 of 3 rise away, 140k Bragg at 17000), but the two muon arms leave 17004 at 180 deg (identical principal-frame slopes) so the collinear trap drops it a tier.
Rule 1, 2 of 2: clean 71-deg V with a 360k stopping-proton Bragg at 8000 and the pi+ rising to 80k at 8001, both cooling to 8002.
Rule 3 excludes 7000 (150k Bragg with a 20 cm Michel on that same end), leaving 7001 as the only cool end with 1 of 1 rising away, but it sits on the y=+200 face so I am close to guessing.

Rule 1 read off the profiles, not the 5 cm means: all three prongs start near 30k at deg-3 4003 and rise away, it is the lowest-z point of the cluster and the prongs spread only 34 deg, all forward in z.
One 216 cm segment and two 0.3 cm specks; rule 1 gives 19001 as the cool end (51k vs a 175k Bragg at 19000) and rule 2 agrees on z, but 19001 is on the y=-196 face and there is no junction anywhere.
A 2.4 cm 86k proton stub sits at 14000 and the 51 cm muon leaves it cool (52k) and rises monotonically along the template to a 155k Bragg at 14002, which carries the 18.6 cm Michel (rule 3).
Rule 1, 3 of 3 at a deg-3 star with well-separated directions: a 71 cm proton to a 176k Bragg, a 28.9 cm pi+, and a 62 cm muon stopping at 125k with an 8.2 cm Michel on it.

Two-Bragg-ends trap resolved: the 230k rise over the last 10 cm at 11001 and the 3-4x MIP 18 cm stub ending 176k at 11000 both point away from 11004, which is 2 of 2 on rule 1 and carries the vertex charge blob.

Rule 1 x2.62: a 12 cm proton leaves 26013 at 92k and stops in a 241k Bragg, and a second 7 cm prong starts 1.2 cm away, both forward in z; the other region's deg-3 hub 18008 has every prong hotter at it.

The 190k spike at the 14004 end collapses to 12k within 3 cm, so it is a vertex blob and not a Bragg, while the far end 14002 rises gradually over 10 cm to 125k and carries the 17 cm Michel-like segment.
Deg-6 hub and the only point in the event with several prongs rising away (3 of 6, including the 158 cm forward track and a 17 cm proton); the principal-frame star radiates from here.

Rule 1 leaves only 17000 once the 215k Bragg at 17001 is excluded, but its 12303 e/cm is anode charge loss (the profile climbs from zero over the first 8 cm), not real cooling, and nothing else is in the event.

Rule 1, 3 of 3 and the only such vertex in the cluster: a 17 cm proton leaves at 130k and stops in a 212k Bragg at 24001, plus a pi+ and a 14.8 cm e both cooling back to 24004, at the lowest-z junction.
